solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Hit performance by current politician (6)

blocks.note: I is the symbol for electric current

annotation.surface: A review of a politician's smash-hit turn, as if an MP had gone on stage.
annotation.walkthrough: 'By' here means 'next to', so the pieces sit together; the order is set by the answer, with current and politician placed before the performance.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a blow or collision, the force of one thing striking another.

entries.clue: Mobilises poorly, accepting pawn is hopeless (10)

indicators.note: the letters of MOBILISES are put together badly, so rearranged
the anagram takes in the P

blocks.note: P is the chess notation for pawn

annotation.surface: A chess player's sorry verdict: the pieces are badly deployed and even giving up a pawn cannot save the game.
annotation.walkthrough: The chess surface makes 'pawn' look like part of the story, but it is just the letter P added to the anagram.
annotation.definitionFit: Something impossible is hopeless: there is no chance of it.

entries.clue: Show underwear with nothing covering bottom (5)

indicators.note: the O takes the place of the last letter, the bottom of a down entry

blocks.note: PANTS, with its bottom letter S replaced

annotation.surface: An order to show off your underwear with nothing on your backside, a cheeky bit of exposure.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Show' looks like a verb (display the underwear) but is the noun. A panto (pantomime) is the British Christmas stage show for families, full of slapstick and cross-dressing.
annotation.definitionFit: Short for pantomime, a British Christmas stage entertainment, so a show by example.

entries.clue: Shy and hollow little laugh (7)

indicators.note: a hollow word has had its insides removed, leaving only its outside letters

blocks.note: to shy is to throw, or chuck

annotation.surface: A timid person's weak, empty little laugh.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shy' looks like an adjective for the laugh, but it is the verb meaning throw, as in a coconut shy.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a quiet, suppressed laugh.

entries.clue: Periodically, news reporters love coffee (8)

indicators.note: take the letters at regular intervals: every second one

annotation.surface: Journalists, it seems, love their coffee from time to time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Periodically' works only on 'news', not the whole phrase, which a solver might try first.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a small, strong black shot made by forcing steam through ground beans.

entries.clue: Dismisses retracted line at end of letter (5)

indicators.note: drawn back, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: to fire is to dismiss from a job

annotation.surface: An employer sacks someone, takes back what they wrote, and ends the letter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Letter' in the surface sounds like correspondence; in the definition it is a printed character.
annotation.definitionFit: A serif is the small stroke finishing a line of a printed letter.

entries.clue: Are bull flies cause of mild rash? (7)

indicators.note: the letters fly about, landing in a new order

annotation.surface: Asks whether the flies around a bull give it a rash.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flies' reads as the insects pestering a bull; it is the verb, telling the letters to scatter.
annotation.definitionFit: Rubella, German measles, is a viral illness whose symptom is a mild rash.

entries.clue: Record of performance scratched on outside of motor (9)

indicators.note: SCORED is placed on the outside, around CAR

blocks.note: to score a surface is to scratch it

annotation.surface: A record of how a car's paintwork was scratched.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface's scratched paintwork suggests a damaged car, but 'performance' points to sport: a card on which a round or innings is recorded.
annotation.definitionFit: A scorecard records how a player or team performed.

entries.clue: Unlock old enclosure (4)

blocks.note: O is a standard abbreviation for old
a pen is an animal enclosure

annotation.surface: An instruction to unlock an old pen or pound.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface points at the gate of an enclosure, which is where the answer belongs too.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to unfasten a door or gate so it can swing wide.

entries.clue: Two mates finally dropping down the hatch (4-4)

indicators.note: each word loses its final letter

blocks.note: china = mate, from rhyming slang 'china plate'; two of them, each losing its last A

annotation.surface: Two friends at the bar, one after the other falling down drunk into the hatch.
annotation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' means mate, so a mate is a china. Chin-chin and down the hatch are both toasts said before drinking.
annotation.definitionFit: Chin-chin is a toast, like 'down the hatch'.

entries.clue: Bureaucrat training new parking attendant (9)

blocks.note: P is the road-sign letter for parking

annotation.surface: An official in charge of training a new car park attendant.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Parking attendant' reads as one job, but it splits into P and USHER.
annotation.definitionFit: A penpusher is a clerk or bureaucrat doing dull paperwork.

entries.clue: Penniless guy changes side (5)

indicators.note: L (left) is swapped for R (right)

blocks.note: BLOKE, with its L to be switched
the other side: R for right replaces L for left

annotation.surface: A man with no money switches political sides.
annotation.walkthrough: A bloke is British slang for a man. 'Side' means left or right, so BLOKE's L becomes R.
annotation.definitionFit: An informal synonym: without a penny to your name.

entries.clue: Present royal fellow less well, faced with absurd cost (8,6)

indicators.note: the letters of COST are made nonsense of, so rearranged
the anagram goes in front of the rest

annotation.surface: A royal who has taken ill is confronted with a ridiculous bill.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a verb, but it is the gift. A stocking filler is a small Christmas present put into a child's stocking.
annotation.definitionFit: A kind of present: a small gift tucked into the Christmas stocking a child hangs up.

entries.clue: Company information is possibly dealt with there (10)

indicators.note: the letters could possibly be arranged otherwise

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters: DEALT with THERE

annotation.surface: A remark that company data is perhaps handled at some place.
annotation.walkthrough: 'With' simply joins the two words of fodder together.
annotation.definitionFit: A letterhead carries a company's name, address and other details at the top of its notepaper.

entries.clue: Problem children (5)

blocks.note: a matter in dispute or a difficulty
a person's offspring, in the formal legal word

annotation.surface: Difficult children, the parents' lament.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Issue' for offspring is formal and legal, as in 'died without issue'.
annotation.definitionFit: Issue means both a problem and a person's children.

entries.clue: Carol free, wanting some time, to choose (6,3)

indicators.note: lacking, so the T is removed

blocks.note: to free is to let out; the T goes
T = time, removed from LET OUT

annotation.surface: Someone named Carol is at liberty but, short of time, must make a choice.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Carol' looks like a woman's name; it is the verb meaning sing.
annotation.definitionFit: A phrasal synonym: to pick one person or thing from a group for special attention.

entries.clue: Charts do not reveal cases blown apart (3,6)

indicators.note: HIDE encases the other letters
the letters of APART are blown about, so rearranged

blocks.note: to hide is to not reveal

annotation.surface: Maps and charts that keep secret cases that have been blown wide open.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cases' looks like a noun (legal cases) but is the verb: HIDE cases the jumbled APART, giving HI(TPARA)DE.
annotation.definitionFit: A dated name for the weekly ranking of best-selling pop records, the charts.

entries.clue: Rotate bed to accommodate a renegade (8)

indicators.note: the bed takes the A inside it

blocks.note: a cot is a small bed

annotation.surface: Turn the bed around to make room for a deserter.
annotation.walkthrough: The A sits inside COT, giving CO(A)T.
annotation.definitionFit: A turncoat is someone who deserts to the other side, a renegade.

entries.clue: Proprietor’s path runs around rolling hill (9)

indicators.note: LANE and R go around the hill

blocks.note: R = runs, the cricket scorecard abbreviation
a down is a rolling chalk hill in southern England

annotation.surface: A proprietor's footpath winding around a rolling hill on the estate.
annotation.walkthrough: '’s' stands for 'is'. LANE + R makes LANER, which goes around DOWN: LAN(DOWN)ER. The Downs are the rounded grassy hills of southern England.
annotation.definitionFit: A proprietor in the particular sense of someone holding an estate or acres.

entries.clue: Inappropriate milieu for after-school networking? (7)

blocks.note: OB = old boy; old boys network after leaving school
a scene is a milieu or setting

annotation.surface: Wonders whether a certain setting is unsuitable for old pupils making contacts.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'old boy network' is the British web of contacts among former pupils of a school; OB SCENE is the place for it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, at its strongest: offensive to decency, grossly unsuitable.

entries.clue: Trainee section of designated activity is over (5)

indicators.note: the answer is a section of the letters that follow
turned over, so read backwards

annotation.surface: A trainee's allotted task has ended.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer lies across the gap between the two words and runs right to left.
annotation.definitionFit: A cadet is a trainee, especially in the armed forces or police.

entries.clue: Prudence raising hundred in sale (7)

indicators.note: in a down entry, the C is moved up to the top

blocks.note: AUCTION with its C lifted out

annotation.surface: A careful bidder putting a hundred up at a sale.
annotation.walkthrough: AUCTION already holds the C; moving it to the top of this down entry gives CAUTION.
annotation.definitionFit: Caution is prudence, care to avoid risk.

entries.clue: Mysterious event left drilling company with spotted work surface (5,9)

indicators.note: a drill bores into something, so L goes inside CO

blocks.note: a kitchen counter is a work surface

annotation.surface: An oil company leaves an unexplained incident behind, drilling through a stained worktop.
annotation.walkthrough: A close encounter is a UFO sighting or contact with aliens, as in the film Close Encounters of the Third Kind.
annotation.definitionFit: A close encounter is a mysterious sighting of an alien craft.

entries.clue: Social media platform stops recording about foreign resident (5)

indicators.note: X plugs the gap, stopping it like a cork
turned about, so read backwards

blocks.note: X is the platform formerly called Twitter

annotation.surface: A social media site shuts down a recording about an expat.
annotation.walkthrough: X goes inside the reversed tape: E(X)PAT.
annotation.definitionFit: An expat (expatriate) lives abroad, a foreign resident.

entries.clue: Start to cheat, breaking honest agreement (5)

indicators.note: take the first letter of cheat
breaking a word splits it open, so the C sits inside TRUE

annotation.surface: Beginning to cheat means breaking an honest deal.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a moral about deals; 'agreement' at the end is the definition, not part of the story about cheating.
annotation.definitionFit: A specific agreement: one between enemies to stop fighting for a time.

entries.clue: Creep uncovered financial records (4)

indicators.note: the covering first and last letters are removed

blocks.note: a ledger is a book of accounts; drop L and R

annotation.surface: A sneaky person has exposed secret accounts.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Creep' reads as a noun, a nasty person; it is the verb, as in to edge forward.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: to move forward slowly and carefully.

entries.clue: Lots of people went by car, perhaps (5)

blocks.note: a crowd moving together, like a herd of cattle

annotation.surface: Crowds of people who travelled by car.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' allows for other vehicles: one drives a bus or a lorry too.
annotation.definitionFit: A drove is a large moving crowd, and drove is also the past tense of drive.

entries.clue: Page with space for truism (9)

blocks.note: latitude is space or freedom to act

annotation.surface: A page with room left for a trite remark.
annotation.walkthrough: Latitude here is scope or leeway, not the map line.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: a remark so obvious and overused it says nothing.

entries.clue: Request agreement, in French first (8)

indicators.note: first means at the front, so EN comes before TREATY

annotation.surface: A plea for an agreement, first drafted in French, the language of diplomacy.
annotation.walkthrough: French is the old language of diplomacy, which is why an agreement drafted 'in French' feels natural in the surface.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an earnest plea or appeal.

entries.clue: Where ownership details can be checked, to be sure (6)

definitions.text: Where ownership details can be checked

blocks.clueFragment: Where ownership details can be checked
blocks.note: a deed is the legal document recording who owns a property, and the details are in it

annotation.surface: Where to look up property records, just to be sure.
annotation.walkthrough: The first half is cryptic: split the answer as IN DEED, the place ownership is written down.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses: an emphatic 'certainly', and literally inside the title document of a property.
